package_info.why_malicious: This version of the package is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution (RCE) due to the behavior of the InvokerTransformer class, which allows attackers to execute arbitrary code via deserialization of untrusted data. This vulnerability (CVE-2015-7501) enables attackers to embed malicious content and trigger code execution through Java reflection.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: InvokerTransformer transformer = new InvokerTransformer("exec", new Class[] { String.class }, new Object[] { "calc.exe" });
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code leverages the InvokerTransformer class to invoke arbitrary methods (such as Runtime.getRuntime().exec()), allowing execution of attacker-supplied code when a crafted object is deserialized.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The ability to invoke arbitrary methods via deserialization is a classic vector for remote code execution attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal deserialization should not allow execution of arbitrary code or system commands. This behavior violates the expectation that data deserialization is safe and does not trigger code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Reflection and method invocation are legitimate in frameworks and libraries, but not in the context of deserializing untrusted data.
key_indicators: Ability to execute system commands (e.g., Runtime.getRuntime().exec())

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a serialized object containing a malicious InvokerTransformer payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deserialization of the object by a vulnerable application.

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable application deserializes the attacker-supplied object, triggering the InvokerTransformer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary code execution on the target system.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of untrusted data containing InvokerTransformer references
Unexpected invocation of Runtime.getRuntime().exec() during object deserialization
Use of reflection to invoke arbitrary methods on deserialized objects
file_indicators: Presence of commons-collections-3.2.1.jar in the classpath
Serialized objects containing InvokerTransformer or similar gadget chains
network_indicators: Outbound connections initiated by deserialized payloads (if attacker code triggers network activity)
Unusual command-and-control traffic following deserialization events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for deserialization of untrusted data, especially when commons-collections-3.2.1.jar is present. Look for use of InvokerTransformer in serialized objects and unexpected system command executions. Use static analysis to flag code paths that deserialize data without validation. Employ runtime monitoring for reflective method invocation and process creation during deserialization.
